ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows two resonance structures inside brackets with a negative charge, with a double-headed resonance arrow in the middle. In the left structure, the sulfur atom has a double bond with the oxygen above, a single bond with the oxygen on the left, and also a single bond with the oxygen on the right that is connected to hydrogen. In the right structure, the sulfur atom has a double bond with the oxygen on the left, a single bond with the oxygen above, and still a single bond with the oxygen on the right that is connected to hydrogen. Reasoning: The upper S-O bond is a double bond in one resonance form and a single bond in the other resonance form, so the average bond order is 1.5. The left S-O bond is a single bond in one resonance form and a double bond in the other resonance form, so the average bond order is also 1.5. The S-O bond connected to hydrogen is only a single bond in both resonance forms, so the average bond order is 1. The larger the bond order, the shorter the bond length. Therefore, the upper and left two S-O bonds are equal in length and shorter, while the S-O bond in S-OH is longer.

method.method_draft: Identify the three sulfur-oxygen bonds in the two displayed resonance structures. For the upper S-O bond, note it is double in one contributor and single in the other, so its average bond order is 1.5. For the left S-O bond, note it is single in one contributor and double in the other, so its average bond order is also 1.5. For the S-O bond to the protonated oxygen, note it is single in both contributors, so its average bond order is 1. Since bond length decreases as bond order increases, conclude that the upper and left S-O bonds are equal and shorter, while the S-OH bond is longer.

method.method_draft: First separate the three S-O bonds into two classes visible in the Lewis diagram: the two S-O bonds to non-H-bearing oxygens that trade the S=O double bond between resonance forms, and the S-O bond to the O-H group that never receives the double bond. Because the first two bonds participate equivalently in the same delocalized pi bond, they must have identical lengths and partial double-bond character. The S-OH bond is a localized single bond and therefore longer. State the comparison as two identical shorter S-O bonds and one longer S-O bond.
